about: A menu of approaches, not rules. Each dimension is one creative decision; each option is a way sources actually do it, with what it is good and bad at. The 35 clashes in CLASHES.md are kept open on purpose: they show up here as options side by side. When ideating, pick one option per dimension and read its looks_like to see the reel it produces.

dimensions.name: Hook method
dimensions.question: How much do we engineer the opening lines?

options.name: Triple hook: context, lean, snapback
options.what: The topic is said, shown and written in the first words. The second line gives a reason to keep watching. The third line pulls the viewer the opposite way.
options.looks_like: Frame 1: the object is on screen, the topic is in big text, and the same words are spoken. Line 2 adds a number or a pain ('...and it's why your shoulders aren't growing'). Line 3 flips it ('The fix isn't lighter weight.'), with a punch-in and a thud. The body then pays off the flip.
weak_at: can feel formulaic if every reel uses it
options.how: Write the three lines before filming. In Edits/CapCut, put the context text on frame 1 under the spoken line and add a punch-in plus a hit on the snapback.

options.name: Say something crazy and get into it
options.what: No hook formula. Open with the boldest honest line you have and start the content at once.
options.looks_like: The first second is a blunt line straight to camera with no setup text ('I'd never buy a gaming laptop again'). There's no title card and no context line. The reasons start on the next breath, and the energy carries it.
weak_at: context can arrive late and raise skips
options.how: Record three or four different openers in one take and keep the strongest. Only trims and captions in Edits.

options.name: Statement, reason, re-hook, 'Why?'
options.what: Briar's live build: a strong statement, a one-sentence reason, a stronger re-hook with higher stakes, then 'Why?' to open the next loop.
options.looks_like: 'Most PC shops overcharge beginners.' (statement) 'They know you won't check the RAM speed.' (reason) 'And I've seen it cost people ₹15,000.' (re-hook) 'Why?' The answer runs through the middle of the reel, and a new loop opens at about 15 s.
weak_at: needs a real stake to escalate
long hooks can drag in short reels
options.how: Write four short lines. Edit the 'Why?' as its own beat (a hard cut or a text pop) so it reads as a turn.

options.name: Three hooks at once: title, verbal, visual
options.what: Design the text hook, the spoken hook and the visual hook as three separate pieces that land together.
options.looks_like: The top text says one thing ('8 GB GPU = ₹50,000 wasted'). The spoken line says a related thing ('Shops still push this card'). The visual is an action (the GPU box slammed on the desk, or a retention graph). Each channel adds something instead of repeating.
weak_at: three things to design and sync
options.how: Plan the three hooks in the script. Build the title in CapCut/Edits text, or as a HyperFrames title card, timed to the visual action.

options.name: Cold open on later highlights
options.what: A long video opens on a fast montage of its best later moments before the start.
options.looks_like: The first 30–50 s are the most extreme lines and shots from later in the video, cut fast with music. Then a title, and the slower main body begins. Viewers know the payoff exists before they commit.
options.how: After the main edit, pull 5–8 peak moments and cut them on beats in CapCut, or as an ffmpeg concat with a music bed.

options.name: Proven template, fill the blanks
options.what: Keep a bank of hook templates with blanks ([X], [Y], [niche]) taken from reels that went viral, each with its proof; pick one and fill it for your idea.
options.looks_like: Before scripting, Srijan fills three templates for the same idea ('Never build a PC if…', '10 saal ka PC pain in 60 seconds', 'This is exactly what you wanna see…'), keeps the strongest and rewrites the words in his own Hinglish with his real numbers.
weak_at: anyone can use the same line (C34)
formulaic if every reel uses it
proof of the template is someone else's views
options.how: Swipe file (template | example link | views | niche) in the Brain or Notes. Fill 3 per idea, then run L09's tests (visualise, falsify, nobody else) on the winner.

dimensions.mixes: Triple hook and the three-channel stack combine naturally (the context line is the title). Briar's statement-reason-rehook is a triple hook that keeps going. A cold open can end on a triple hook. A filled template can be the context-lean of a triple hook; Srijan's own numbers and self-roast are what make it 'nobody else could say it'.
dimensions.pick_by: Short teaching or proof reels: triple hook or the three-channel stack. Raw yaps or volume weeks: say something crazy. 60 s and up: statement-reason-rehook. Long form: cold open. Blank page or a busy week: template bank, then rewrite in your voice.

dimensions.name: Hook type
dimensions.question: What kind of first line or first image is it?

options.name: Contrarian take / 'Don't buy X'
options.what: Open with something most people believe and say it is wrong, or tell them not to buy or do the obvious thing.
options.looks_like: 'Don't buy the RTX 5070 at ₹2 lakh.' The price is on screen and a red DON'T BUY stamp lands on the box in the first second. The rest gives the better alternative.
weak_at: pure debunks can leave the viewer with nothing (Rahul's weakest reel)
options.how: Say the take in the first line. Add a stamp or strike-through graphic in CapCut, or a HyperFrames stamp card.

options.name: Curiosity question or 'do this now'
options.what: Ask about a pain the viewer has, or give them a tiny action to try while watching.
options.looks_like: 'Does your animation look robotic?' over a robot-vs-pro side-by-side. Or 'Put your phone on airplane mode right now...' while the code keeps changing on screen. The answer is held back until the middle.
weak_at: the payoff must be worth the wait
options.how: Put the question as text on frame 1 with the spoken line. For 'do this now', show the exact steps in a screen recording.

options.name: Contrast: looks X, sounds Y / before vs after
options.what: Two things side by side, or a two-part line that sets up the problem in one glance.
options.looks_like: Top text: 'Looks pro.' Then: 'Sounds like this: 🔇' over a silent clip. Or a split screen: wrong form left, right form right. The viewer gets the gap before a word of explanation.
options.how: Split-screen layout in CapCut/Edits, or two text lines that pop in sequence with a pop SFX.

options.name: Proof or verdict first
options.what: The result, number or verdict comes in the first second, with no intro.
options.looks_like: 'Core i9 14900K. ₹46,000. 3 out of 10.' The product card, price and score pop in one after another in the first second. Or a myth quoted as text while the lift that disproves it is already moving.
weak_at: gives the answer away early, so the body needs its own pull
options.how: Start the edit on the proof frame. Add the number card or score in CapCut, or as a HyperFrames counter.

options.name: Undercut a paid offer
options.what: Play or quote a rival's strongest line, then undercut it: 'He sells this for $97. I'm giving it away free.'
options.looks_like: A rival's clip plays in a card: 'I didn't edit a single second of this video.' A $97 checkout card pops onto it. Cut to you: 'I'm giving it away for free.' Every step is then explained.
options.how: Rival clip in a rounded card (CapCut overlay or HyperFrames), a price card on the word, then your face full frame.

options.name: Expertise hook: years of X in 60 seconds
options.what: Template '[N years] of [niche] in [60 seconds]'. Authority plus time compression in one line: my years, your minute.
options.looks_like: Frame 1: Srijan at the rack, text '4 SAAL KA GYM TRAUMA / 60 SECONDS' while he says it. A fast blitz of the mistakes follows, one per cut. Adam's example: '3 years of therapy in 60 seconds' (40.5M).
good_at: context and lean in one line
sets up a fast list body
weak_at: the body must actually feel condensed
options.how: Say it in the first second with the number and niche as on-screen text. Cut the body as a blitz (one lesson per 2–3 s) with n/5 badges in CapCut or HyperFrames.

options.name: Warning hook: never start X without these N things
options.what: Template 'Never start a [X] if you don't have these [Y] things'. A prohibition on a big step, gated by a counted checklist the viewer checks themselves against.
options.looks_like: 'Never build a gaming PC if you don't have these 4 things.' Four number tiles pop in (1-2-3-4) and a red '4 THINGS' lands. Each item gets one shot and one reason. Adam's example: 'Never start a business if you don't have these 4 things' (339K).
good_at: open loop (which things? do I have them?)
ends with something useful, unlike a pure debunk
weak_at: preachy if the items are generic
needs 3–4 items that are really needed
options.how: Number tiles or n/4 badges in CapCut or HyperFrames, a hit SFX on the count word. Keep each item to one line plus a reason.

options.name: Desire hook: this is exactly what you want to see
options.what: Template 'This is exactly what you want to see when you're [situation]'. 'This' points at the ideal outcome on screen; the situation lets the right viewer self-select.
options.looks_like: Frame 1 is the proof: a spotless second-hand GPU with the warranty seal intact, temps 62°C. Voice: 'This is exactly what you wanna see jab tum second-hand GPU kholte ho.' Adam's example: an aerial warehouse with a map pin, 'when you're buying an industrial property' (3.6M).
weak_at: needs the real thing to film
options.how: Open on the proof shot, not your face. Put the situation as text on frame 1 so the context isn't late. A funny snapback line can follow ('…aur mummy bolti hai kuch fark nahi pada').

options.name: Promise hook: daily habit, three payoffs
options.what: Template 'If you [do B] every single day, you're going to [X], [Y] and [Z]'. A tiny repeatable habit with three stacked, concrete outcomes.
options.looks_like: Srijan scoops creatine or laces up for a walk; the three payoffs pop as text one by one on the beat, the third one is the joke ('…aur Sunday ki biryani guilt-free'). Adam's example: creatine, 'build more muscle, recover faster…' (28M, the biggest in the reel).
weak_at: health claims need to be true
generic if the habit is obvious
options.how: Write three payoffs that are concrete and true. Pop each as text with a pop SFX in CapCut/Edits, or HyperFrames kinetic text.

dimensions.mixes: Any of these can sit in the 'lean' slot of a triple hook. Proof-first plus contrarian ('3/10, don't buy') is Rahul's usual pairing. Contrast is the visual form of a contrarian take. L11's four templates slot into a triple hook: Expertise and Promise are context + lean in one line; Warning is a contrarian take that opens a checklist; Desire needs a proof visual from frame 1.
dimensions.pick_by: Debate and comments: contrarian. Saves on how-tos: curiosity or contrast. Ratings and proof reels: proof-first. Free alternatives to paid things: undercut. Authority and a fast list body: expertise. Saves on a big decision: warning. Proof footage of the ideal result: desire. Habits and gym: promise.

dimensions.name: Hook lean
dimensions.question: After the context, what makes the viewer want the next sentence?

options.name: Proof: a stat, screenshot or result
options.what: Back the context at once with a number, screenshot or visible result.
options.looks_like: Context line, then a retention graph, a GitHub star count ticking up, or the plate count on the bar. The viewer sees it is real before the explanation.
weak_at: dry numbers without a story feel flat
options.how: Screenshot or screen-record the proof. Add a number counter (HyperFrames or CapCut keyframes) and a highlight on the key line.

options.name: Pain point or benefit
options.what: Name a specific struggle the viewer has, or the outcome they want.
options.looks_like: 'Your Claude edits look pro but sound like a silent movie.' Or '...without paying for Photoshop.' The line makes the viewer feel the problem is theirs.
weak_at: needs to be specific to land
options.how: Write the pain in the viewer's own words, taken from comments or Reddit. A caption pop is enough.

options.name: Shocking or unexpected fact
options.what: An unexpected image, statement or fact. L01 counts it as a valid lean; Caleb calls it 'getting a little tiresome'.
options.looks_like: Context line, then 'Your 2FA code works with Wi-Fi off.' The phone in airplane mode keeps changing the code on screen. A surprise that makes the viewer stay to learn why.
weak_at: feels clickbait if the fact is weak
options.how: One line plus a visual proof of the fact. B&W freeze or punch-in on the reveal.

options.name: Bold contrarian statement
options.what: Lean with a belief that goes against the crowd. Caleb prefers this over unexpected facts.
options.looks_like: Context: 'Gym progress.' Lean: 'Your program doesn't matter as much as you think.' The viewer stays to see if you can defend it.
weak_at: must be defended in the body
can alienate if it's just provocation
options.how: Say it to camera with a punch-in. Use the '8 Mile' structure in the body to answer the obvious objection.

options.name: Odd pattern interrupt
options.what: Something strange in the frame or the line that breaks the scroll before it makes sense.
options.looks_like: 'I eat blueberries like it's my job... you missed the first 30.' Or an odd object planted in frame that people will comment about. The weirdness is the lean.
weak_at: the topic still has to arrive fast
options.how: Plan the odd detail in the shot list, or open on the oddest frame you filmed.

dimensions.mixes: Proof plus contrarian is the strongest pairing (a bold line backed at once). Pain plus proof is the classic tutorial lean.
dimensions.pick_by: Trust and saves: proof or pain. Comments: contrarian or pattern interrupt. Reach with a fresh fact: shock fact, used sparingly.

dimensions.name: Hook clarity
dimensions.question: Must everyone get the opening instantly, or can it be for insiders?

options.name: Understood in one Mississippi
options.what: Anyone scrolling past understands the topic in about 2 s, through words, picture and text together.
options.looks_like: A plain line, a plain picture, the same words as text: 'Khandala, 2 hrs from Pune'. A stranger with half their attention still knows what the reel is.
options.how: Test the first line on someone who doesn't follow the niche. Put the topic word in big text on frame 1.

options.name: Not everyone gets it
options.what: Write for the people who know. Harry: 'if everyone gets it, you're possibly doing something wrong.' Inside jokes and niche language.
options.looks_like: 'Bulking season starts and suddenly everyone's a powerlifter.' Gym people laugh, outsiders scroll on. Comments fill with people who get it.
options.how: Use the niche's own words in the hook and the caption. Keep the edit simple; the line does the work.

options.name: Line 1 teases, line 2 explains
options.what: The first line's only job is to get the second line read. A small mystery is cleared up by about 2 s.
options.looks_like: Line 1: 'This ₹500 thing beat my ₹15,000 upgrade.' Line 2, a second later: 'A better thermal paste.' Brief confusion, then a clear topic.
weak_at: if line 2 is late, it becomes unclear
options.how: Two text pops about 1 s apart with a pop SFX each. Carousel: slide 1 teases, slide 2 explains.

dimensions.mixes: Instant-clear topic plus an insider line in the body keeps reach and community. A two-step reveal is a short-delay version of instant-clear.
dimensions.pick_by: Reach and non-followers: instant-clear. Community and comments: insider. Curiosity without losing clarity: two-step.

dimensions.name: Claim size
dimensions.question: How big a claim do we make?

options.name: Small, sincere, provable
options.what: A modest claim the viewer can check. It is believable because it isn't big.
options.looks_like: 'This cut my render time from 4 minutes to 3.' The timer is shown on screen. Nothing is 'insane'; the number does the work.
options.how: Run each line through visualize / falsify / nobody else. Show the proof object.

options.name: Bold claim, instant proof
options.what: A big claim in the hook, backed on screen within 2–3 s.
options.looks_like: 'Scientifically impossible to skip.' A retention graph appears at once. The boldness grabs attention and the proof keeps the trust.
weak_at: backfires if the proof is weak
options.how: Prepare the proof graphic first. Cut to it on the claim's last word.

options.name: Best or worst: green or red, never grey
options.what: Call something the best or the worst and defend it. Keep nuance for private work.
options.looks_like: 'Lamington Road is the worst place to buy your first PC.' Then two reasons and a story. People who disagree argue in the comments.
weak_at: needs a belief you really hold
options.how: Talking head with a punch-in on the take. A 'hook, story, two points' script.

options.name: Bold reel with an honest limitation
options.what: Make the strong claim, then admit one real limit ('the honest part...') so the rest is believed.
options.looks_like: Three tools sold hard, then: 'The honest part: it only ships 78 sounds.' The admission sits two-thirds of the way in and makes the earlier claims feel safe.
options.how: Add one 'honest part' beat to the script. Mark it with a small text label.

dimensions.mixes: A strong take whose evidence is small and checkable gets both: a loud hook and a sincere body.
dimensions.pick_by: Trust and saves: small sincere or bold-plus-limit. Comments: strong take. Thumb stop with proof ready: bold with proof.

dimensions.name: Core idea type
dimensions.question: What kind of thought is the reel built on?

options.name: Strong take
options.what: An opinion stated hard and defended.
options.looks_like: Sitting at the desk: 'Mechanical keyboards are overrated for gaming.' Two reasons, one story, done in 40 s.
weak_at: repetitive if every reel is a take
options.how: Standard yap on a tripod. Jump cuts and captions in Edits.

options.name: Strong take, then teach
options.what: Use the opinion as the hook, then pivot to a lesson.
options.looks_like: 'Too many people skip warm-up sets.' Then a quick breakdown of a warm-up ladder, with the sets on screen. It opens like an argument and ends like a tutorial.
weak_at: the pivot has to feel natural
options.how: Script: take, '8 Mile' objection, steps. Use graphics for the steps.

options.name: Small epiphany
options.what: A relatable everyday observation ('do you notice how...').
options.looks_like: 'Have you noticed everyone at the gym films the last rep, never the first?' Nods of recognition. It's short, warm and very sendable.
options.how: Take it from the Yap Map. One take, captions, maybe one B-roll insert.

options.name: Story time
options.what: A real story: hook, problem, messy middle, lesson. Origin and failure stories work best.
options.looks_like: '3:47 a.m., Khandala, and the bus has left without us.' Time, place, what went wrong, then what you learned. Hinged on 'but' and 'so' rather than 'and then'.
options.how: Script: hook, problem, journey, lesson, CTA. Show B-roll of the place or moment.

options.name: Humour / poke fun
options.what: Something funny, or gentle mockery of a shared enemy (shop markups, gym bros, overrated places).
options.looks_like: Sarcastic congratulations: 'Wow, ₹75,000 for your first PC...' with a B&W freeze and a meme cutaway. Or a deadpan meme-audio skit.
options.how: B&W freeze or meme cutaway in CapCut on the punchline. Trending meme audio is added in Edits.

dimensions.mixes: Oren: takes, small epiphanies and stories cover 90% of content. A story can carry a take (hook, story, two points), and humour can sit on top of any of them.
dimensions.pick_by: Comments: strong take. Saves: take to education. Shares: epiphany or humour. Trust and follows: story time.

dimensions.name: Content mechanism
dimensions.question: What is the reel's engine: teaching, testing, ranking, busting, or a series?

options.name: Tutorial / do-this-now
options.what: Teach one thing the viewer can apply at once, ideally while watching.
options.looks_like: A screen recording of the exact steps, with a circular face cam: 'Change one word in the Gmail URL...'. The result appears on screen and the viewer tries it.
options.how: Screen-record on the PC/iPhone. Show each step with a click SFX and a highlight box in CapCut.

options.name: Myth-bust / proof reel
options.what: Quote a myth, then disprove it, ideally with a physical demo.
options.looks_like: Text: 'Pilates won't make you stronger.' A weighted plank is already in motion. 6–18 s, with the text on screen the whole time and a loop-friendly end.
weak_at: a debunk with no takeaway underperformed for Rahul
options.how: One or two shots on a tripod, bold quote text in Edits, trending audio low under it.

options.name: Challenge / experiment
options.what: A clear premise you test: 'I tried X for 7 days', 'X vs Y', 'I tested the cheapest...'.
options.looks_like: Cold open on the most extreme moment, then 'let's find out'. Stages with a scoreboard or day counter, and a verdict at the end.
options.how: Plan the stages and film each with the same angle and light. Add a HyperFrames scoreboard or day counter. Hook template (L11): 'I'm going to [X] for [Y] days straight' (example: study 8 hours, 5 days straight, 4.9M).

options.name: Rating, tier list or versus
options.what: Score things, rank them, or put two against each other.
options.looks_like: Product card, price, then the x/10 reveal with a one-word label ('HEATER'). Or '6 ways A beats B', posted with the mirror version 48 h later.
options.how: Score cards and tier tables in HyperFrames, or CapCut text with a pop SFX per score. Hook template (L11): 'Rating [X] so you don't waste your [Y]' (example: supplements / money, S–F tier board, 4.7M).

options.name: Series / monthly franchise
options.what: Recurring episodes: 'Day X of...', or a dated franchise like '₹X PC Build – October 2026'.
options.looks_like: Same opener, same angle, same title style every episode, with a day counter or month label. The ending says 'follow along'. Each episode stands alone but rewards followers.
weak_at: fatigue if the format never changes
options.how: Build a template project in CapCut or a HyperFrames title card with the day or month as a variable.

dimensions.mixes: A series of tutorials or ratings (Rahul's monthly builds) combines two engines. A myth-bust is often the hook of a tutorial.
dimensions.pick_by: Saves and shares: tutorial. Follows: series or experiment. Comments: rating/versus or myth-bust (with a takeaway).

dimensions.name: List approach
dimensions.question: Do we use lists, and what kind?

options.name: No generic lists
options.what: Skip 'top 3' and 'three ways to'; build on takes, epiphanies and stories instead.
options.looks_like: Instead of '3 chest exercises', one opinion: 'Dips build more chest than bench for most people.' One idea, defended.
weak_at: loses an easy, proven reach format
options.how: Turn each list idea into one take, then use the Yap Map.

options.name: 4–5 mini takes
options.what: A list where every item is a strong take: 'Observations I made at X as a Y'.
options.looks_like: '5 things I noticed at my first LAN event.' Each item is a 6–10 s mini video with its own opinion, and the viewer stays for the next one.
options.how: Number each take with an n/5 badge. A whoosh plus a punch-in at each new item.

options.name: Numbered blitz / utility listicle
options.what: Rapid-fire useful items: '9 travel hacks', '3 tools'. Tristan: even 'here's three things' beats no frame.
options.looks_like: 1/3, 2/3, 3/3 badges pop in. Each item gets 5–8 s with a visual and a pop SFX. A summary card at the end invites a screenshot.
weak_at: generic if the items are common knowledge
options.how: HyperFrames progress badges and item cards, or CapCut text templates. Keep one visual per item. Hook template (L11): 'These are the 5 best ways to use [X]'; flash the numbered menu in the first 2 s.

options.name: Rating / tier list
options.what: A list where each item gets a score or tier, ending on the full table.
options.looks_like: Six CPUs, each with a price and an x/10 verdict. The full tier table flashes at the end (sometimes held back for a comment CTA).
weak_at: the table can be too small to read
options.how: HyperFrames tier board or chart. Score reveal with a hit SFX. Open with 'Rating [X] so you don't waste your [Y]' (L11).

options.name: List as a carousel
options.what: Put the list in slides instead of a reel. Caleb saw listicles do better as carousels.
options.looks_like: Slide 1 hook, slide 2 a second hook, then one image plus one or two sentences per item. Readers swipe at their own pace and save it.
options.how: 1080×1350 slides from Canva or HyperFrames stills. One idea per slide.

dimensions.mixes: A list of takes is the bridge between both sides (structure plus opinion). A reel blitz can be waterfalled into a carousel list.
dimensions.pick_by: Reach and saves: blitz or carousel. Comments: tier list or list of takes. Personality and trust: no lists.

dimensions.name: Teaser vs give everything
dimensions.question: Does the reel give the whole thing, or hold some back?

options.name: Give everything, right here
options.what: The full answer is in the video. 'Share the knowledge, sell the execution.'
options.looks_like: Every step is shown, with a 'take a picture' pause on the full map at the end. Nothing is held for DMs.
options.how: Hold the final summary frame for 2–3 s. Say 'everything is here, no DM needed'.

options.name: Show part, comment for the rest
options.what: Show some of the list or answer, then 'comment X for the rest'.
options.looks_like: Six CPUs rated, then the full tier list flashes for half a second. 'Comment CPU for the full list.'
options.how: End on a fast flash of the full asset plus a keyword label. Deliver it by DM.

options.name: Give it all, DM the extra
options.what: The video explains everything; the DM gives a bonus (exact settings, a file, styling).
options.looks_like: Every step is explained on screen. The CTA: 'Comment EDIT and I'll send the exact styling I used.' Nobody feels cheated and the comments still come.
options.how: Prepare the bonus (preset, PDF, link list) before posting. The keyword is shown on screen at the end.

options.name: Hyper-edited teaser for a long piece
options.what: A 30–45 s cut of the most contrarian soundbite, sending people to the full video.
options.looks_like: Black screen, glowing text, then the guest's wildest line, shots under 2 s, bass hits on text pops, a thud and a cut to black. 'Full episode on YouTube.'
weak_at: needs a long piece behind it
options.how: Pull one soundbite, cut on percussive hits in CapCut, and add push-ins and a glow on the text.

dimensions.mixes: Give-all-plus-extra sits between both sides. A teaser for a long piece is the one case where holding back is the whole point.
dimensions.pick_by: Trust and saves: give everything. Comments and leads: withhold or extra. Long-form traffic: teaser.

dimensions.name: Audience width
dimensions.question: How wide or narrow is the audience the hook calls out?

options.name: Widen one layer
options.what: Raise the audience one level for reach ('PC builders' becomes 'anyone with a laptop') and drop narrowing words.
options.looks_like: Not 'RTX owners, do this' but 'Your laptop is wasting battery because of one setting.' Anyone can relate in the first second.
good_at: universal topics travel furthest (Rahul's Gmail reel)
weak_at: ghost followers who don't care about the core niche
options.how: Rewrite the hook without niche words, then test it on a non-niche friend.

options.name: Hyper-specific or hyper-local
options.what: Call out an exact place, moment or person: 'If you're going to Nehru Place this weekend...'.
options.looks_like: Road-sign graphics with real market names. The hook names the exact situation, and the right viewer feels it was made for them.
options.how: Name the exact place in the hook, the on-screen text, the caption and the location tag.

options.name: Start narrow, expand in layers (80/20)
options.what: Be great at one thing first, then add adjacent topics; 80% core, 20% other interests.
options.looks_like: Most reels sit on one pillar with one look. Every fifth one stacks a side interest (gym plus tech: 'the apps I track my lifts with'). The account reads as one clear thing.
options.how: Tag each idea core or side and keep the ratio. No production change.

options.name: Wide on top of funnel, narrow lower down
options.what: Reach posts go wide; teaching and selling posts go narrow. Briar splits them this way.
options.looks_like: A wide relatable reel brings strangers in. A narrow 'blow their mind' breakdown for the core audience follows. Each post knows its job.
weak_at: wide posts can still attract ghosts
options.how: Label each idea TOFU, MOFU or BOFU before scripting.

dimensions.mixes: Rahul's sample shows both: universal tricks got the most reach, niche builds the best like rates. Interest stacking widens without abandoning the core.
dimensions.pick_by: Reach: one layer up. Loyal engagement: hyper-specific. Long-term brand: narrow then layers. A mixed weekly plan: split by funnel.

dimensions.name: Language
dimensions.question: Which language do we speak and write in?

options.name: English speech and text
options.what: Everything in English.
options.looks_like: English voice, English captions and caption copy. It reads cleanly to a global or pan-India audience.
options.how: Auto-captions in Edits/CapCut, or faster-whisper word timings for custom captions.

options.name: Hinglish speech, English captions
options.what: Talk naturally in Hindi/Hinglish while labels and captions stay in English (Rahul's pattern).
options.looks_like: 'Achchha, October mein ek lakh ka PC?' spoken, with 'DON'T BUY' and '₹1,00,000' in English on screen. It feels local and still scans fast.
options.how: Whisper language 'hi' for timing, then write English labels by hand in CapCut.

options.name: Hinglish throughout
options.what: Hinglish voice and Hinglish (Roman script) captions.
options.looks_like: Captions read 'Aapko pata hai Gmail mein sirf ek word badlo...' word by word. It sounds like a friend talking.
options.how: Write the captions by hand; auto-captions mangle Hinglish.

options.name: Switch by theme
options.what: Choose per post: chill or local posts in Hinglish, teaching or global posts in English.
options.looks_like: A travel vibe reel with a Hinglish caption ('chill scenes'), next to an English tech explainer. The language matches the mood.
options.how: Decide the language in the copy pack, before writing.

dimensions.mixes: Hinglish speech with English labels is itself a mix. Captions can switch even when the voice doesn't.
dimensions.pick_by: Global reach: English. Indian tech and personality: Hinglish speech with English text. Local warmth: Hinglish throughout.

dimensions.name: Post caption length
dimensions.question: How long is the written caption under the post?

options.name: Short: two lines or less
options.what: Every word earns its place. No paragraph over two lines.
options.looks_like: One hook line, one value line, a CTA, and 3–5 tags. It reads in two seconds above 'more'.
weak_at: less room for SEO and story
options.how: Write it, then cut every word that can go (pull-out test).

options.name: Long candid note
options.what: A personal note that rewards readers ('I don't know if any of you read the caption...').
options.looks_like: The first line hooks, then several paragraphs about what happened behind the reel, ending with a question. Readers comment about the caption itself.
options.how: Write it like a letter: time, place, what happened. Keep the paragraphs short.

options.name: Structured: hook, value, CTA, keywords
options.what: A template: a keyword hook line, 1–3 lines of story or value, a send/save CTA, and 3–5 precise tags.
options.looks_like: 'Khandala sunset point nobody stops at' as line 1 (searchable), two lines of context, 'Send this to the colleague who...', a location tag and 4 hashtags.
options.how: Use the copy-pack template, and put the place or keyword in the first 125 characters.

options.name: Long, but in short paragraphs
options.what: Rahul's length with Harry's rhythm: a long caption made of one- and two-line paragraphs.
options.looks_like: Eight short paragraphs, each one or two lines, like monkey bars. It's long but easy to swing through on a phone.
weak_at: still a lot of writing per post
most viewers still won't open it
options.how: Draft it in the Instagram caption box to see the real line breaks.

dimensions.mixes: All can share the same first line; only what comes after 'more' changes.
dimensions.pick_by: Fast or vibe posts: short. Story or personal posts: long candid. Search-driven travel or tips: structured. Trust-heavy posts: long in short paragraphs.

dimensions.name: CTA approach
dimensions.question: What does the end of the reel ask the viewer to do?

options.name: Comment KEYWORD, get it by DM
options.what: 'Comment HOOKS and I'll send it to you.' A freebie by DM, ideally a living resource.
options.looks_like: The last 3 s show a big keyword label, then a mock comment box typing the word and a DM preview with the freebie ('Verified part list · LIVE PRICES').
options.how: Keyword label and a mock comment-to-DM graphic in HyperFrames or CapCut. Same keyword in the caption.

options.name: No DM needed, it's all here
options.what: Say plainly that nothing is held back, and give a 'take a picture' save moment.
options.looks_like: 'No DM for resources, everything you need is right here.' At the end the full step board is held on screen: 'I'll leave it here so you can take a picture.'
options.how: Hold the summary frame 2–3 s at the end. Say the line in the hook or the outro.

options.name: Conversation CTA: your takeaway
options.what: Ask for a reflective comment ('comment your biggest takeaway') rather than a keyword. No selling.
options.looks_like: The last line: 'Which of these would you try first? Tell me below.' No freebie, no DM, just a question that invites a real reply.
options.how: End on the question as text plus voice. Pin your own answer as the first comment.

options.name: Send this to...
options.what: Ask the viewer to send the reel to a specific person or team.
options.looks_like: 'Send this to the friend who always says one more set.' The final text names the person type, and the reel itself is something you'd forward.
weak_at: only works if the reel is relatable
options.how: Put it in the caption and as an end text. Name a specific person type.

options.name: To a landing page or email list
options.what: Send people somewhere you own: bio link, newsletter, lead magnet page.
options.looks_like: 'The full checklist is in my free newsletter, link in bio.' The bio's three lines end on the sign-up. Fewer comments, but each lead is reachable by email.
weak_at: needs a page and an email setup
options.how: Set up a landing page plus a lead magnet first. Weekly 'comment X for my free course' can feed it.

dimensions.mixes: Briar's weekly lead magnet mixes keyword and owned list (comment, then email). Give-all-plus-extra mixes anti-CTA trust with a keyword. Share and conversation CTAs can sit on reels that sell nothing.
dimensions.pick_by: Comments and leads: keyword DM. Trust and saves: anti-CTA. Meaningful engagement: conversation. Reach: share CTA. Sales: owned list.

dimensions.name: CTA frequency
dimensions.question: How often do posts ask for something or sell?

options.name: A keyword CTA on nearly every reel
options.what: Every reel ends with a comment keyword and a freebie.
options.looks_like: Ten reels in ten days, each ending on its own big yellow keyword (75K, CPU, GMAIL). The audience learns that every reel has something to collect.
weak_at: a freebie to make every time
options.how: Keep a keyword plus freebie template in HyperFrames, and a resource folder ready for DMs.

options.name: Weekly rhythm: 4 reach, 2 deep, 1 sell
options.what: Most posts are reach or value; one a week sells. Stories sell twice a week, the rest is life.
options.looks_like: Four wide, relatable reels with no ask, two deep breakdowns with a soft ask, and one 'sneak peek inside' post with a clear offer. Stories sell on Tuesday and Friday.
options.how: Tag each planned post TOFU, MOFU or BOFU in the content plan.

options.name: Rarely sell in organic content
options.what: Organic content builds trust; selling happens elsewhere (long form, email, the bio).
options.looks_like: Reels end on a takeaway question or nothing at all. The offer lives in the bio and the newsletter.
options.how: Use conversation or share CTAs only. Selling is in the bio line 3.

dimensions.mixes: Every reel can carry a free keyword (not a sale) while selling stays weekly, so the two are compatible when the freebie is free.
dimensions.pick_by: Comments and lead lists: every reel. Balanced growth plus sales: weekly rhythm. Pure brand building: rarely sell.

dimensions.name: Comment and DM handling
dimensions.question: Who answers comments and delivers DMs?

options.name: Auto-DM on keyword
options.what: A tool (ManyChat-style, parked as P4) sends the freebie when someone comments the keyword.
options.looks_like: The viewer comments 'CPU' and gets a DM with the link within seconds, even at 2 a.m. or at 2,000 comments.
options.how: Parked tool (P4); not set up. A manual copy-paste DM is the stand-in.

options.name: Reply yourself
options.what: You reply to commenters personally, even if only a few a week. Teams reply only under a labelled account.
options.looks_like: Within the first hour every comment gets a real reply, inside jokes included. Commenters come back because you answered.
options.how: Block 15 minutes after posting. Note repeated questions as future topics.

options.name: Auto-deliver, personal replies
options.what: The freebie arrives automatically; conversations and comment replies stay personal.
options.looks_like: The DM link lands instantly. You still reply to the first 20–30 comments yourself and answer follow-up DMs in your own words.
options.how: Our inference; it depends on whether P4 is approved.

dimensions.mixes: Hybrid is the combination. At low volume, personal handling of the keyword DMs is the same as hybrid.
dimensions.pick_by: Low volume: personal. Viral keyword reels: automation or hybrid.

dimensions.name: Posting cadence
dimensions.question: How often do we post?

options.name: About one reel a day
options.what: Daily posting, with occasional doubles, at fixed time slots.
options.looks_like: Ten reels in ten days at 10–11:30 or 17:30–19:30 IST. Series episodes and timely reels keep the feed fresh.
weak_at: quality per reel drops without a team
options.how: Batch-film, keep templates, and keep a bank of finished reels.

options.name: Three a week, pillar system
options.what: At least 3 expert posts a week: 3–5 formats, each 3–4 times a month (12–16 posts), reviewed monthly.
options.looks_like: Monday a tutorial, Wednesday a take, Friday a carousel, every week. At month end you compare pillars and swap the weakest after two bad months.
options.how: A pillar calendar with a format label on each slot. About an hour of review a month.

options.name: Accordion: volume first, then effort
options.what: Post a lot early to learn what the audience calls quality, then fewer, bigger pieces.
options.looks_like: Months 1–3: rough, 'just trimmed' reels most days. Later: three highly produced pieces a week that carry what the volume phase taught.
weak_at: needs honest review to know when to switch
options.how: Set a date or follower milestone to compress.

options.name: Sustainable baseline and a bank
options.what: A rate you can always hit, backed by a bank of 14–15 ready videos and a fixed daily filming hour.
options.looks_like: A promise like 3 shorts a week that never slips, because two weeks of reels are already edited. Filming happens in one protected hour.
weak_at: the bank can go stale on timely topics
options.how: Keep evergreen reels in a 'bank' folder and timely reels separate.

dimensions.mixes: An accordion can start daily and settle into a pillar system. A bank makes any cadence steadier.
dimensions.pick_by: Learning fast: daily or accordion. Brand quality: three a week. Unpredictable weeks: baseline plus bank.

dimensions.name: Cross-posting
dimensions.question: Does one cut go everywhere, or is each platform edited separately?

options.name: Master one, cross-post the rest
options.what: Get good on one network (usually Instagram) and post the same file everywhere because it compounds.
options.looks_like: One reel goes to Instagram, Shorts, TikTok and LinkedIn the same day with the same hook. It costs nothing extra.
weak_at: hits a ceiling on each platform
watermarks or originality issues if exported badly
options.how: Export a clean master (no watermark) and upload it natively to each app.

options.name: Native re-edit per platform
options.what: Same footage; the meat stays and the hook changes per platform.
options.looks_like: The Instagram cut opens with a text hook, the Shorts cut opens on the action, and the TikTok cut is rawer. Same body, three openings.
options.how: Keep the body as one sequence. Swap only the first 3–5 s per export in CapCut/ffmpeg.

options.name: Waterfall one long piece
options.what: Make one long piece and cut it into 10+ clips, carousels and posts.
options.looks_like: One YouTube video becomes six reels, two carousels, a quote card and a story series. Each piece links back to the long one.
good_at: short form for awareness, long form for conversion
options.how: Transcribe with faster-whisper, pick self-contained moments, and reframe to 9:16 with an OpenCV tracker.

options.name: One platform in focus at a time
options.what: 2–3 platforms, but resources go to one while the others sit in maintenance mode, then rotate.
options.looks_like: Instagram gets custom edits and daily replies; YouTube gets reposts only, until it is its turn.
weak_at: slow to build a second audience
options.how: Pick the focus platform for the quarter, and cross-post to the rest.

dimensions.mixes: Oren's own path mixes them: cross-post first, then build per-network strategies (level 2).
dimensions.pick_by: Speed: same everywhere. Growth ceiling: native re-edit. Long-form makers: waterfall. Limited time: one platform at a time.

dimensions.name: Success metric
dimensions.question: Which number tells us a post worked?

options.name: Hook rate and skip rate first
options.what: Did people stay past the first seconds? The opening is judged above everything.
options.looks_like: Two reels with the same body but different openers; the one with the lower skip rate wins, and its hook style is reused.
weak_at: for ads it 'doesn't really matter' if ROAS hits
options.how: Instagram Insights skip rate and 3-second views. Trial Reels to test openers.

options.name: Multiple of your own baseline
options.what: Score each post against the median of your last 75–90 days, per format.
options.looks_like: A sheet: this reel is 1.8×, that one 0.6×. 'Viral for you' is about 4–5×. The monthly top 10% is studied for what they share.
options.how: Log the numbers about 11 days after posting. Update the benchmark monthly.

options.name: Sends and saves (one goal per video)
options.what: Decide before posting whether the reel is for sends, saves or comments, and judge it on that.
options.looks_like: A relatable reel is judged on sends per reach; a tutorial on saves. Likes are ignored.
weak_at: sends and saves show only in Insights
options.how: Write the goal in the edit blueprint and check Insights after 24–72 h.

options.name: Conversions: leads, sales, ROAS
options.what: Only metrics that change actions: sign-ups, sales, return on ad spend.
options.looks_like: A reel with fewer views but 40 email sign-ups beats a viral one with none. Ads are judged on ROAS, not thumb stop.
options.how: UTM links or keyword counts per reel; ad maths in Meta Ads Manager.

options.name: Untangle: one variable at a time
options.what: Split each video into hook, format, topic and illustration, and change one per week.
options.looks_like: Same topic and format, new hook style this week; next week same hook, new format. The cause of a win becomes visible.
options.how: Tag each post's four parts in a sheet.

dimensions.mixes: The multiplier sheet can carry any of these columns. Hook rate for organic and conversions for ads is how Oren splits it.
dimensions.pick_by: Testing openers: hook rate. Fair trend reading: multiplier. Ranking signals: sends and saves. Business: conversion. Learning why: untangle.

dimensions.name: Research method
dimensions.question: Where do ideas and references come from?

options.name: Study one same-niche creator deeply
options.what: Download and measure one creator's reels: cuts, beats, loudness, hooks, CTAs.
options.looks_like: Twelve reels measured with ffmpeg and Whisper, giving a table of what this creator does every time and what drives their outliers.
options.how: yt-dlp for study only, then ffmpeg scene detection, EBU R128 loudness and contact sheets.

options.name: 5 in-niche for topics, 5 outside for packaging
options.what: Take topics from niche peers and formats, angles and series from creators in other niches.
options.looks_like: A gym topic packaged like a finance creator's whiteboard series. Nobody in the niche has seen that combination.
options.how: Keep two saved collections on Instagram: topics and packaging.

options.name: Study the viewer's whole feed
options.what: You compete with everything in the feed. Make an account that follows what your ideal viewer follows, and copy only true outliers.
options.looks_like: Fifteen minutes a day scrolling a second account full of skits, memes and creators the audience loves. Ideas come from what beats its own creator's average.
options.how: A second Instagram account. Note outliers at 2× or more of their creator's average.

options.name: Audience questions and niche forums
options.what: Ideas from repeated comment and DM questions, objections, and top posts in niche subreddits.
options.looks_like: Five people ask 'which RAM for this board?' and that becomes a reel. A top-of-month subreddit thread becomes a myth-bust.
weak_at: needs an audience or forum access
options.how: Log repeated questions weekly. Summarise top subreddit posts with AI.

options.name: Trend scan
options.what: Track trending formats, audio and release dates across niches, and adapt the format rather than copying the video.
options.looks_like: A weekly report: GTA 6 countdowns, a gym myth-rebuttal proof reel, a trending sound at 'growing' stage. Pick one and add your own flavour.
weak_at: can pull away from your core
options.how: Run the researcher (brain/research/RESEARCHER.md); trends.json holds the output.

dimensions.mixes: Deep study gives craft; the 5+5 and whole-feed methods give packaging; questions give topics. They answer different parts of an idea.
dimensions.pick_by: Craft benchmarks: one creator deep. Fresh packaging: 5+5 or whole feed. Proven demand: audience questions. Timely reach: trend scan.

dimensions.name: Planning level
dimensions.question: How much is decided before the camera rolls?

options.name: Storyboard every beat
options.what: A table with every line, what's on screen, which tool, and the sound cue, agreed before shooting or editing.
options.looks_like: A 24-row table: '01 · 0:00–0:02.8 · I didn't edit a single second · hook text from frame 0 · SCORE: drop on Claude did.' The edit matches the plan.
options.how: Prompt Claude for the table (# / time / say / on screen / tool / sound cue) and approve it before 'build it'.

options.name: Light script from a framework
options.what: Bullet points from a frame (hook, story, two points; or 8 Mile), and several versions of the hook.
options.looks_like: A notes-app card with a hook line and three bullets. Five hook versions are written side by side and the best is picked.
weak_at: less precise sound and visual timing
options.how: Use the frameworks from L06. Write 4–5 hook versions and get feedback.

options.name: Improvise with pauses (ReCut)
options.what: Talk freely; pause in silence to think; cut the silences later and re-record the intro at the end.
options.looks_like: A 6–7 minute raw take cut down to 60 s of the best lines. The intro was recorded last, when warmed up.
options.how: Silence removal in CapCut (or the ReCut app), then jump cuts and captions.

options.name: Press play and just post
options.what: Minimal planning: turn the camera on, say the thing, post it.
options.looks_like: A camera-on, step-back clip shot in one go. Sometimes these are the best performers.
options.how: One take and auto-captions in Edits.

dimensions.mixes: A storyboard can be written after an improvised take (plan the edit, not the talk). Script frameworks fit inside improvising.
dimensions.pick_by: Effect-heavy or AI-built edits: storyboard. Talking reels: light script or ReCut. Volume weeks: press play.

dimensions.name: AI's role
dimensions.question: What job does AI do in making the content?

options.name: AI as editor
options.what: Give Claude a reference reel and the raw footage; it edits in that style; you give feedback in words; then turn it into a skill.
options.looks_like: Raw footage goes in and an edit with cuts, captions, cards and sound comes back. You say 'tighter at the start, less zoom' and get v2.
weak_at: can look generic without a good reference
options.how: ffmpeg, faster-whisper, OpenCV and HyperFrames via Claude Code. Save the workflow as a skill.

options.name: AI writes the plan, you approve
options.what: AI drafts the storyboard or blueprint; a human fixes it; then AI or a human builds it.
options.looks_like: Claude proposes a 20-beat table, you change six rows and approve it, and the build follows the table.
options.how: Storyboard prompt from L10, then 'build it'.

options.name: AI for ideas and research only
options.what: AI finds unique, specific, observed situations and does research; the human writes and performs.
options.looks_like: Ask: 'What's the most specific situation a beginner PC builder has lived?' Get 20 situations, pick one, and write it in your own words.
options.how: Chat prompts for ideation; WebSearch for facts.

options.name: AI for craft jobs (sound, motion, measuring)
options.what: AI handles specific craft: placing SFX, easing curves, word timings, measuring reference reels.
options.looks_like: You cut the reel. AI adds a pop on every text frame, eases the zooms, and checks loudness at −14 LUFS. The creative calls stay yours.
weak_at: AI can't hear, so it needs a listening check
options.how: real-sfx and earshot skills, the four-line easing prompt, faster-whisper.

dimensions.mixes: They stack: AI for ideas, a human script, an AI storyboard, then an AI edit with craft tools. Harry and Briar draw the line at writing; L04 and L10 hand over editing.
dimensions.pick_by: Speed on repeat formats: AI editor. Effect-heavy pieces: AI planner. Voice and originality: ideation only. Polish on a human edit: craft helper.

dimensions.name: Using other creators' content
dimensions.question: Do other people's reels appear in ours, and how?

options.name: Original only
options.what: No reposts or near-duplicates; trends are adapted as formats.
options.looks_like: Every frame is our own footage or graphics. A trending format is rebuilt with our own shots and voice.
options.how: Use references only as study; rebuild the look ourselves.

options.name: Pause-and-play breakdown
options.what: Play another creator's reel in a card, freeze at each effect, and explain how to make it.
options.looks_like: The source plays top-right with its audio, freezes, and shrinks beside your head while you explain the effect. About a quarter of the runtime is the source.
options.how: Source in a rounded card (CapCut overlay or HyperFrames), with freeze frames on each beat.

options.name: Commentary proven on your own footage
options.what: Reference the other reel briefly, then apply each effect to your own shot as you name it.
options.looks_like: A short glimpse of the source, then the grade sliders move and your own saturation drops on screen. Most of the runtime is your footage.
weak_at: still shows some of the source
options.how: Rebuild each effect on your clip in CapCut, ffmpeg or HyperFrames, timed to the spoken word.

options.name: Study privately, remake the style
options.what: Download references for analysis only, then make your own video in that style.
options.looks_like: The viewer never sees the reference. They see your reel with the same pace, layout and caption style.
options.how: yt-dlp to the scratchpad only, then a reference-driven edit.

dimensions.mixes: Pause-and-play is safer when most of the runtime is commentary proven on your own footage.
dimensions.pick_by: Default reach safety: original only or study-then-remake. Teardown teaching: commentary with own demo, with pause-and-play as the riskier, punchier version.

dimensions.name: On-screen caption style
dimensions.question: How do the burned-in captions look, if there are any?

options.name: Word by word, key word in a coloured box
options.what: One word or phrase at a time; the key word sits in a coloured highlight box.
options.looks_like: White bold words flip every 0.3–0.5 s and 'speed.' lands inside a red box. The eye locks onto the box each time.
weak_at: 'lose the green box' (L10) says it looks less clean
options.how: CapCut auto-captions with the highlight template, or faster-whisper timings into HyperFrames captions.

options.name: Plain white with soft shadow, no box
options.what: White bold sans, soft drop shadow, 1–3 words, no background box.
options.looks_like: Small clean words sit just above the lower third, at about 61% height. They read easily without fighting the picture, and one coral box appears only for a special word.
options.how: Edits/CapCut captions with the box off and a shadow on; HyperFrames text-shadow for custom builds.

options.name: Uppercase caption bar between halves
options.what: Uppercase bold white captions, 3–4 words, placed on the seam of a split screen.
options.looks_like: Face on top, step board below, and a strip of caps words running across the middle. The eye sits where both halves meet.
options.how: Caption track positioned at the split line in CapCut, all caps, 3–4 words per card.

options.name: Custom kinetic text (not captions)
options.what: Only key words animate in as designed type with glow, scale pops and tracking, instead of full captions.
options.looks_like: '$100,000/MONTH' slams in with a glow and a bass hit, then 'WHY' alone. Most words are not written; the important ones are big.
options.how: HyperFrames kinetic type blocks, or CapCut text with keyframed scale and glow.

options.name: No burned captions, title only
options.what: No captions on the body; a title card carries the topic. Oren's own long form does this.
options.looks_like: A clean talking shot with a yellow serif section title when each part starts. Nothing scrolls along the bottom.
weak_at: Oren recommends captions for almost everybody in short form
options.how: Title cards only; YouTube's closed captions for accessibility.

dimensions.mixes: L10 uses plain captions with one box moment. Kinetic key words can sit over plain captions. Short form with captions and long form without is the reading C4 offers.
dimensions.pick_by: Retention-first short form: highlight box. Premium or clean look: plain shadow. Split layouts: caption bar. Teasers: kinetic. Long form: title only.

dimensions.name: Font pairing / type style
dimensions.question: What typefaces and colour accents do titles and labels use?

options.name: Clean sans, red/green coding
options.what: Inter or SF Pro style, white and yellow on dark; red means wrong, green means right.
options.looks_like: Plain white labels, a green tick on the right way and a red cross on the wrong. Nothing decorative; it reads like a good app.
options.how: The system sans in Edits/CapCut, or Inter in HyperFrames, with two accent colours.

options.name: Serif accent plus sans body
options.what: Emphasis words or section titles in a serif (italic or bold yellow), body in clean sans.
options.looks_like: 'Looks *pro*.' with 'pro' in serif italic, and yellow serif section titles between parts. It feels editorial and a bit premium.
weak_at: serifs get thin on small screens
options.how: Instrument Serif Italic plus Inter in HyperFrames; Edits/CapCut have similar serif options.

options.name: Extended wide sans, neon highlights
options.what: Extended bold geometric titles (Druk Wide or Monument Extended style), Inter body, cyan, lime and pink on numbers.
options.looks_like: Wide heavy 'ROAS' fills the width; numbers glow cyan and lime on black. It feels like a tech launch.
options.how: A free extended display font plus Inter in HyperFrames; CapCut has a wide display font.

options.name: Brush script plus heavy extruded sans
options.what: Brush-script accents paired with a heavy condensed or extruded sans, red and cyan palette.
options.looks_like: 'If I have to make' in script, then '$100,000/MONTH' in heavy caps with glow and chromatic aberration. It feels like a hype trailer.
options.how: Montserrat ExtraBold plus a free brush script; glow via CapCut effects or a HyperFrames filter.

options.name: Heavy condensed caps labels, one accent
options.what: 1–3 word all-caps condensed labels in a single brand accent (Rahul's yellow) on black boxes; big ₹ figures with shadow.
options.looks_like: 'WI-FI OFF', 'HEATER', '₹46,000' pop over the chest in yellow on black. Instantly recognisable as one creator's look.
options.how: Bebas or Oswald style caps in Edits/CapCut with a black box; one brand hex for every label.

dimensions.mixes: Most sources pair one display face with a clean sans body. Condensed caps labels plus clean sans captions is Rahul's combo; serif emphasis plus sans is L02 and the Khandala reel.
dimensions.pick_by: Teaching: clean sans. Travel and premium: serif plus sans. Tech brand look: extended neon or condensed caps. Hype teasers: script plus heavy.

dimensions.name: Colour grade look
dimensions.question: What overall colour mood does the footage have?

options.name: Warm golden
options.what: Warm, golden mids with soft highlights; for travel, warm temperature with the sun's disc kept.
options.looks_like: Skin glows, sunsets stay orange without clipping, and greens aren't neon. Inviting and nostalgic.
options.how: Edits/CapCut temperature and saturation sliders; Khandala ffmpeg recipe (S-curve, R +0.03, saturation 1.10).

options.name: Moody, desaturated
options.what: Highlights pulled down, blacks lifted, saturation −15%, soft vignette.
options.looks_like: A dim desk lit by a warm lamp, colours muted, soft shadows. Serious, filmic, late-night.
good_at: focus on the face and text
options.how: ffmpeg curves, eq=saturation=0.85 and a vignette; or Edits/CapCut highlights −35, blacks +12, saturation −15.

options.name: High contrast with neon accents
options.what: Deep blacks, high contrast, saturated cyan, magenta and amber accents.
options.looks_like: RGB lights pop against black, the face is crisp, edges are punchy. It looks like a launch event.
options.how: Contrast up and blacks down in CapCut/VN, with saturation boosted on accent hues only (HSL).

options.name: Cool, contrasty, textured
options.what: Neutral to cool, higher contrast, clarity up for muscle definition, distracting signage desaturated.
options.looks_like: Muscles show texture under side light, the gym looks clean and steely, and bright signage fades into the background.
options.how: A saved preset per pillar in CapCut, with a safe and a bold version and an orange-HSL skin check.

options.name: Dark matte with one accent colour
options.what: Near-black background, warm key on the face, and one brand accent colour everywhere.
options.looks_like: A dark room, a warm-lit face, and every label, ring and banner in the same yellow (or red). It's recognisable at thumbnail size.
options.how: Light the face warm against a dark set; pick one hex accent for all graphics.

dimensions.mixes: L08 grades the teaser high-contrast and the body natural. Grades can be set per pillar (gym cool, travel warm) under one accent colour.
dimensions.pick_by: Travel: warm golden. Desk and tech talk: moody or dark-matte. Setups and launches: neon contrast. Gym: cool contrasty.

dimensions.name: Grade blacks
dimensions.question: Are the blacks lifted, deep, or in between?

options.name: Lifted, soft blacks
options.what: Blacks raised (+12), highlights pulled down, for a soft, filmic matte.
options.looks_like: Shadows look dark grey rather than black, and nothing is crushed. Gentle and moody, like a film still.
options.how: Edits/CapCut 'Blacks' slider +12, or an ffmpeg curves black point lift.

options.name: Deep, high-contrast blacks
options.what: True blacks and strong contrast so accents and highlights pop.
options.looks_like: Black is black, and lights and text glow against it. Punchy on OLED phones.
options.how: Blacks down and contrast up in CapCut/VN; watch the skin with the HSL orange check.

options.name: Slight lift, neutral
options.what: A gentle S-curve with shadows lifted only a little: contrast without crushing.
options.looks_like: It reads as natural with a bit of polish. Shadows keep detail and the image still has bite.
weak_at: can look plain next to bold grades
options.how: The Khandala ffmpeg recipe (gentle S-curve, contrast 1.04), or small slider moves.

dimensions.mixes: Lifted blacks pair with a moody grade; deep blacks with neon or gym looks. L10 lifts the blacks without crushing (YMIN 7–12).
dimensions.pick_by: Filmic and calm: lifted. Punchy and energetic: deep. Unsure or mixed footage: slight lift.

dimensions.name: On-screen layout
dimensions.question: How is the 9:16 frame divided?

options.name: Full-frame face with pop-up labels
options.what: Waist-up or face full frame, with short labels popping over the chest and punch-ins on emphasis.
options.looks_like: You fill the frame talking; 'HEATER' pops in yellow over your chest and a punch-in lands on the punchline.
options.how: Tripod at eye level; labels and zoom keyframes in Edits/CapCut.

options.name: Framed graphic yap
options.what: Frame yourself low, leaving headroom for a vertical graphic or text behind your head.
options.looks_like: You sit in the lower 60%, and above your head a vertical image, card or title (sometimes behind your head via a cut-out) changes every couple of seconds.
good_at: premium with text behind the head
weak_at: must be framed correctly at the shoot
options.how: Tripod higher, shot wider; overlays in CapCut; text behind the head with a segmentation cut-out (HyperFrames or CapCut auto cut-out).

options.name: Split: graphic top, face bottom
options.what: The top half or ~55% shows an animated graphic or example; your face is underneath; full face for key lines.
options.looks_like: A URL bar animates at the top while you explain below; for the punchline you go full frame. Or wrong form on top, right form below.
weak_at: graphics work for the top half
options.how: CapCut canvas split, or a HyperFrames top-half composition over the face clip.

options.name: Content card plus circular face cam
options.what: A screen recording or source card fills most of the frame with your face in a small circle (PiP).
options.looks_like: A dark rounded card shows the app or article with a yellow highlight; your face sits in a ringed circle bottom-centre with an app badge.
options.how: CapCut mask (circle) on the face clip over the screen recording; HyperFrames for rounded cards and shadows.

options.name: Full-screen content, no face
options.what: The screen recording, native app interface, green-screen image or gameplay fills the frame; voice only.
options.looks_like: The real Instagram or Windows interface being tapped, result first. Or you in front of one green-screen image, talking.
options.how: iPhone screen recording or OBS; voiceover in Edits; green screen via CapCut background removal.

dimensions.mixes: Rahul switches between full face, card plus PiP and meme cutaways every few seconds rather than holding one layout. L01 switches from split to full face for key lines.
dimensions.pick_by: Personality: full face. Teaching with visuals: split or framed. Software and proof: card plus PiP. Demos with no camera: full-screen content.

dimensions.name: Visual density
dimensions.question: How many things are on screen at once?

options.name: One element carries it
options.what: One idea, one image, one line. Neil French: if one element does the job, you're onto a winner.
options.looks_like: A single shot of a sunset with one line of text, held. No labels, no stickers, no meme. It doesn't look like an ad, so people watch it.
weak_at: the one element must be strong
options.how: Pick the single strongest shot and line. Remove everything else.

options.name: Layered: audio, visual and text together
options.what: Say it, show it and write it at once; something changes every 1.5–2.5 s.
options.looks_like: Voice, picture and caption carry the same idea; a new card or cut arrives every two seconds with a sound.
options.how: Plan visual changes on the script every ~2 s; captions on; SFX on the changes.

options.name: Calm camera, busy overlays
options.what: Few camera cuts; cards, freezes and overlays enter and leave about every 2 s.
options.looks_like: One locked desk shot for ~10 s at a time while repo cards, prompt bars and a grade panel slide in on the exact words. Only about six full-frame cuts in 85 s.
options.how: faster-whisper word timings, then HyperFrames cards timed to each word.

options.name: Chaotic: memes, layouts and images every 1–2 s
options.what: Images, memes, layout swaps and labels change constantly.
options.looks_like: Talking head, then a meme with the GPU pasted in, then a parts card, then a B&W freeze, then a road-sign graphic, all within ten seconds.
options.how: About 30 images per 60 s as CapCut overlays; meme cutaways of 1–3 s.

dimensions.mixes: A one-element hook can open a layered body. Harry speaks about print ads, the others about video, so 'one idea per reel, layered delivery' is a common blend.
dimensions.pick_by: Vibe and premium: one element. Teaching: layered or calm camera with overlays. Comedy and energy: chaotic.

dimensions.name: Polish level
dimensions.question: How produced is the reel?

options.name: Full polish
options.what: SFX on every event, easing on every move, counters and badges, a change every 1.5–2.5 s.
options.looks_like: Every text pop has a sound, every zoom glides, numbers count up, cards spring in. It feels like a studio made it.
weak_at: polish can't fix a weak hook
options.how: HyperFrames graphics plus the real-sfx skill, easing curves in CapCut/VN keyframes, and an earshot check.

options.name: Polish the key beats only
options.what: Craft goes into the hook, the punchline and the end; the middle stays simple.
options.looks_like: A designed hook with a music dropout after the punchline, plain captions through the middle, about 10 SFX across 41 visual events, and a styled CTA.
weak_at: you need to choose the beats
options.how: Mark three key beats in the storyboard and polish only those.

options.name: Just trimmed
options.what: Cut the dead air, add captions, post. Quality is what the audience says it is.
options.looks_like: A phone on a tripod, one take, jump cuts, auto-captions. Some of the most viral videos are shot at night on a phone.
options.how: Edits: trim, auto-captions, export. Five minutes.

options.name: Polish by platform
options.what: Candid iPhone footage for TikTok-style feeds; produced edits where the platform rewards them.
options.looks_like: The same idea as a raw iPhone take on TikTok and a designed, SFX-rich cut on Instagram or YouTube.
options.how: Raw export first, then a polished version from the same timeline.

dimensions.mixes: The accordion runs just-trimmed early and full polish later. Caleb's red flag is polish without a hook, not polish itself; his own course is highly produced.
dimensions.pick_by: Learning and volume: just trimmed. Flagship teaching or tech reels: full polish. Most weeks: selective. Multi-platform: by platform.

dimensions.name: Motion style
dimensions.question: How do zooms, pans and graphics move?

options.name: Linear (constant speed)
options.what: Moves start and stop at once and travel at a steady speed.
options.looks_like: A slow steady pan across a landscape photo with no acceleration. It drifts like a security camera; L03 calls it robotic.
good_at: steady slow drift on still photos (our take)
options.how: The default keyframes in CapCut/VN; ffmpeg zoompan with t/d.

options.name: Eased: entrances ease out, exits ease in
options.what: Entrances arrive fast and brake gently; exits start slow and speed away. Nothing linear.
options.looks_like: A card slides in quickly and settles 'as if set down by a steady hand'; a push-in glides and stops softly. It feels professional without being noticed.
weak_at: overshoot on big moves looks wrong
options.how: Ease curves on keyframes in Edits/CapCut/VN; an eased expression in ffmpeg; the four-line easing prompt for HyperFrames.

options.name: Spring with slight overshoot
options.what: UI cards and text pops overshoot a little and settle back.
options.looks_like: A label pops to 105% and settles to 100%; cards bounce in lightly. Playful and app-like.
options.how: The bounce or overshoot preset in CapCut text animations; a spring easing in HyperFrames.

options.name: Static shots, hard cuts
options.what: No camera moves; motion comes only from cuts (and maybe overlays).
options.looks_like: A locked talking shot with jump cuts. Only the overlay windows move.
options.how: Cuts only in Edits; overlays get eased motion.

dimensions.mixes: L03's rule mixes them by job: entrances ease out, exits ease in, UI springs. Hard cuts plus eased overlays is L06's mix.
dimensions.pick_by: Camera moves and big graphics: eased. Text and UI pops: spring. Speed with no moves: static hard cuts. Linear only as a deliberate choice.

dimensions.name: Counter and motion-graphic usage
dimensions.question: Which motion graphics carry information?

options.name: None or minimal
options.what: Footage and captions only.
options.looks_like: Real footage carries everything; at most a title card. Feels natural and documentary.
weak_at: numbers and steps are harder to follow
less to look at in teaching reels
options.how: Captions only in Edits.

options.name: Counters and progress badges
options.what: Numbers count up (weights, prices, stars) and n/3 badges mark list items.
options.looks_like: '75 KG' ticks up from 0 as the bar moves; 1/3, 2/3, 3/3 badges in the corner. The viewer always knows where they are.
weak_at: gimmicky if every reel has one
options.how: HyperFrames counter component; CapCut number templates.

options.name: Data cards, stamps and price strikes
options.what: Parts grids that fill up, receipts, date stamps, price strike-throughs, DON'T BUY stamps, SAVED pills.
options.looks_like: An empty parts grid fills slot by slot with prices while a budget bar grows; the old price is struck through and the new one lands with a stamp.
options.how: HyperFrames price cards and charts; CapCut shapes plus text.

options.name: Proof cards on the exact word
options.what: Screenshots, repo cards and logo cards appear the moment they are named; real screenshots over mock-ups.
options.looks_like: You say 'Whisper' and the GitHub card pops above your head on that syllable, with a highlighter on the key line.
options.how: faster-whisper word timestamps, then HyperFrames cards placed on those times.

options.name: Signature effects: text behind head, B&W freeze, memes
options.what: A few recurring tricks that become part of the look.
options.looks_like: The title sits behind your head; a sarcastic line freezes in black and white; a 2 s meme cutaway has the product pasted in.
options.how: Segmentation cut-out (CapCut auto cut-out or HyperFrames), a desaturate-and-hold freeze, meme overlays.

dimensions.mixes: Rahul uses counters, data cards and signature effects in one reel. L10 uses proof cards plus one signature effect (text behind the head) reused for the CTA.
dimensions.pick_by: Numbers and lists: counters. Prices and builds: data cards. Tutorials: proof cards. Brand recognition: one signature effect.

dimensions.name: Transition style
dimensions.question: How does one shot or section move to the next?

options.name: Hard cuts on beat or motion
options.what: Plain cuts, placed on a beat or on movement.
options.looks_like: Shot changes land on the kick drum or mid-gesture, so they feel invisible.
weak_at: no energy boost on their own
options.how: Cut on beat markers in Edits/CapCut, or on movement.

options.name: Whip pan
options.what: About 5 frames of horizontal motion blur plus a whoosh and hit into the next framing.
options.looks_like: The shot smears sideways for a split second, whoosh, and you are in a new framing. It's energetic but clean; L10 chose it over a recursive zoom.
options.how: CapCut 'whip' transition, or ffmpeg directional blur over 5 frames plus a whoosh SFX.

options.name: Kinetic wipes and board zooms
options.what: Horizontal wipes, text slide-ins or a zoom across a board to the next step, each with a whoosh.
options.looks_like: A wipe carries the next idea in from the right; or the camera glides across a step board to step 3, then pulls back to the whole map at the end.
options.how: HyperFrames wipe blocks; CapCut slide transitions with ease-out.

options.name: Glitch, colour bars, CRT static
options.what: A TV colour-bar glitch or a static burst between sections or chapters.
options.looks_like: A one-frame burst of colour bars, then the next section. Or a chapter card arriving on a CRT TV with static.
options.how: CapCut glitch transitions; HyperFrames CRT and glitch blocks plus a static SFX.

options.name: Reveal moves and trend transitions
options.what: Pan-to-reveal, fan-blade wipe, flip or similar trend transitions; ending on a thud and cut to black.
options.looks_like: The camera pans off the sun to reveal the group, or an object passes the lens to wipe to the next scene. The reel ends on a thud into black.
options.how: Shoot both halves with matching motion; join in CapCut with a mask or match cut.

dimensions.mixes: Most sources use hard cuts for the body and one stronger transition for section changes. L10 skipped the recursive zoom as 'a bit too much'.
dimensions.pick_by: Default: hard cuts. Section changes with energy: whip pan. Step-by-step teaching: wipes. Tech chapters: glitch. Vibe and travel: reveals.

dimensions.name: Edit pace
dimensions.question: How often does something on screen change?

options.name: Hyper: shots under 2 s
options.what: Shots of 0.8–1.8 s, push-ins, flashes and speed ramps on percussive hits.
options.looks_like: Trailer energy: every hit of the beat brings a new shot or push, with text slamming in. Done in 30–45 s.
options.how: Cut to beat markers in CapCut; speed ramps on hits.

options.name: Fast: a change every 1.2–2.5 s
options.what: A cut, label, card or layout swap every 1.2–2.5 s, with no dead air.
options.looks_like: Breaths are cut and every couple of seconds a label pops, the layout flips or a card slides in. Talking, but never still.
options.how: Silence removal, then add a visual event every ~2 s on the timeline.

options.name: Overlay-driven, slow camera
options.what: Camera shots last ~10 s; overlays change about every 2 s.
options.looks_like: The same desk framing holds while cards, prompts and freezes come and go every couple of seconds. Calm but busy.
options.how: Lock the camera; build the overlays in HyperFrames on word timings.

options.name: Measured: 2.5–4.5 s shots
options.what: Talking shots of 2.5–4.5 s, with axial jump cuts on emphasis words and longer holds for demos.
options.looks_like: A conversational rhythm; a punch-in on every few emphasis words and 8–15 s holds while something is demonstrated.
weak_at: can feel slow in short form
options.how: Jump cuts every 3–6 words with digital punch-ins in CapCut/VN.

options.name: Long takes
options.what: Wide multi-cam with long uncut conversation; demos are the pattern interrupts.
options.looks_like: Two people talking in a wide shot for a minute at a time; occasionally a screen demo cuts in.
options.how: Switch angles only on speaker changes.

dimensions.mixes: Train a regular rhythm, then break it for the big moment. Long pieces can open hyper (the teaser) and settle into measured.
dimensions.pick_by: Teasers: hyper. Short teaching: fast or overlay-driven. Long form: measured. Podcasts: long takes.

dimensions.name: Punch-in zoom style
dimensions.question: How do we zoom for emphasis on a talking shot?

options.name: No punch-ins
options.what: The framing never changes within a shot.
options.looks_like: One steady frame per shot; emphasis comes from voice and text only.
options.how: Nothing to add.

options.name: Subtle 105–110%
options.what: A small punch-in on key phrases and at each new section.
options.looks_like: When a new point starts, the frame tightens slightly. The viewer feels it more than sees it.
options.how: Scale 105–110% on the clip after the cut, or a quick eased keyframe.

options.name: Big 1.15–1.3× on punchlines
options.what: A smooth, larger push on punchlines and framework names.
options.looks_like: On the punchline the face fills the frame in a smooth push. It's clearly a 'this matters' moment.
options.how: Shoot 4K for crop room; eased scale keyframes to 115–130%.

options.name: Axial jump cuts every 3–6 words
options.what: Alternate between a medium shot and a digital punch-in on the same angle every few words.
options.looks_like: Medium, close, medium, close, each landing on an emphasis word. A single camera feels like two.
options.how: Alternate the scale on each jump cut in CapCut/VN.

options.name: Push-ins on percussive hits
options.what: 10–15% push-ins and push-outs synced to the music's hits.
options.looks_like: Every drum hit pumps the frame in or out. It feels like a music video.
options.how: Beat markers in CapCut, then a scale keyframe on each.

dimensions.mixes: Subtle punch-ins on sections plus a big one on the main punchline is a common pairing (L06 and L07 differ only in size).
dimensions.pick_by: Talking short form: subtle. Punchlines: big. Single-camera long form: axial. Music-driven edits: beat pushes.

dimensions.name: SFX style and density
dimensions.question: Which sound effects, and how many?

options.name: A sound on every visual event
options.what: Whoosh for movement, pop for text, chime for success, thud or click for impact; UI clicks on screen recordings.
options.looks_like: Every label pops, every slide whooshes, every tick chimes, the final rep thuds. Without it the edit feels like a 'silent movie'.
options.how: Edits/CapCut SFX library, or the real-sfx skill with uisfx cues; earshot to check.

options.name: Sparse accents on key beats
options.what: About 10 SFX across 41 visual events; sound marks only what matters, plus a deliberate dropout.
options.looks_like: Most overlays enter silently. A pop on the price card, a hit on the real screenshot, a whoosh on the whip pan, and half a second of silence after the punchline.
