weak_at: you need to choose the moments
options.how: Plan SFX in the storyboard's SCORE column; place 5–10 by hand.

options.name: Cinematic impacts and risers
options.what: Bass hits on key text, risers and sub-booms at chapter edges, metallic thuds, CRT static.
options.looks_like: A riser builds into '$100,000/MONTH', a sub-boom lands with the text, and a metallic thud ends the reel before black.
weak_at: over the top for casual content
options.how: Risers, booms and hits from CC0 Openverse; placed with real-sfx; checked with earshot.

options.name: Meme stingers
options.what: Vine boom, record scratch, bass drop, scream stingers on reveals and punchlines.
options.looks_like: The weak-looking guy lifts the bar: record scratch, freeze, vine boom. Pure comedy timing.
weak_at: the library is missing for now
options.how: Edits/CapCut meme sound library; our own meme SFX library is not built yet.

options.name: No SFX, dialogue only
options.what: Voice (and maybe music) only.
options.looks_like: A conversation or vlog with no added sounds; the voice carries it.
options.how: Nothing to add.

dimensions.mixes: L07 uses every-event UI sounds plus cinematic chapter impacts. L10 pairs sparse accents with a music dropout. The C13 clash is partly this choice: every event vs selective.
dimensions.pick_by: Graphic-heavy teaching: every event. Clean premium reels: sparse accents. Teasers and hype: cinematic. Comedy: meme stingers. Podcasts: none.

dimensions.name: Music approach
dimensions.question: What role does music play?

options.name: Quiet bed under the voice
options.what: A low lo-fi or ambient bed about −22 to −24 dB, or 7–10 dB under the voice, for the whole reel.
options.looks_like: You barely notice it, but silence never happens. The voice sits on top, clean.
weak_at: generic if always the same track
options.how: A CC0 or in-app track ducked under the voice in CapCut; mix to about −14 LUFS.

options.name: Trending audio added in-app
options.what: A trending song chosen in Edits/Instagram at post time, ideally at the 'growing' stage.
options.looks_like: A vibe or transformation reel cut to a recognisable trending song; the audio page links it to thousands of others.
weak_at: can't be baked into our renders
options.how: Export silent, then pick the track in Edits; check its use count (under ~10K uses is ideal).

options.name: Music-led, cut to the beat
options.what: The music drives the edit: cuts, ramps and text land on beats.
options.looks_like: Every cut hits the kick, the top rep lands on the drop, and the text appears word by word on the beat.
options.how: Beat markers in CapCut/Edits; cut on markers.

options.name: Music changes by section, with dropouts
options.what: Different music per section (driving hook, lo-fi teaching, swell at the outro), plus planned dropouts.
options.looks_like: A driving synth under the hook, a half-second of silence after the punchline, then a softer bed while teaching, and a swell into the final line.
options.how: A SCORE column in the storyboard; crossfade tracks in CapCut, or the real-sound skill.

options.name: Voice only, no declared music
options.what: No trending track; the voice dominates (Rahul lists no track on any reel; L08's body has no bed).
options.looks_like: Just the voice, compressed and loud, maybe a faint room tone. Every word is clear.
options.how: Clean the voice (compress, de-ess, high-pass) and mix to −14 LUFS.

dimensions.mixes: A quiet bed plus a dropout after the punchline is L10's mix. Trending audio low under a voiceover is common in travel. Rahul likely runs a very low bed (inferred from the noise floor) but declares no track.
dimensions.pick_by: Talking teaching: quiet bed or voice only. Vibe, travel and transformation: trending or beat-synced. Story arcs: by section.

dimensions.name: Face vs faceless
dimensions.question: Is a face on camera, and how much?

options.name: Expert on camera
options.what: One person talking to camera; Oren's number-one strategy.
options.looks_like: You, looking into the lens, explaining. The face is the brand.
options.how: Tripod, plug-in mic, standard yap.

options.name: Face as a small cameo
options.what: The content fills the frame; the face sits in a corner circle or appears only for key lines.
options.looks_like: A screen demo with a ringed face circle reacting; full face only for the hook and the CTA.
good_at: face stays visible on screen content
options.how: A CapCut circle mask over the content; film the face separately or with the screen capture.

options.name: Hands-only POV with voiceover
options.what: No face; POV hands doing the thing, with a voiceover and a concept.
options.looks_like: Top-down hands building a PC or loading plates, with a voiceover telling a mini story. Gel Blaster's POV skits hit 800,000 this way.
options.how: Overhead or chest-height phone mount; voiceover recorded separately in Edits.

options.name: Motion graphics only
options.what: Everything is animation and text, with or without voice.
options.looks_like: A dark background, an animated graph with a dotted trail, word-by-word captions. No camera footage at all.
options.how: HyperFrames compositions; voiceover optional.

options.name: B-roll plus text, no voice
options.what: Footage of the day or place with on-screen text and music; you appear but don't talk.
options.looks_like: A timestamped day: 6:00 alarm, 6:40 gym, 9:00 desk, each with a time label, cut to music. Or a travel dump with captions.
options.how: B-roll list per session; text plus trending audio in Edits.

dimensions.mixes: Face for the hook and the CTA with faceless content in between is common (L01 and Rahul switch layouts). A cameo face is the middle ground.
dimensions.pick_by: Trust and follows: face. Tutorials: cameo. Concept skits: hands POV. Abstract explainers: graphics only. Vibe: B-roll plus text.

dimensions.name: Talking format
dimensions.question: If someone talks, in what setting and shape?

options.name: Standard yap
options.what: Sitting, a phone on a tripod, talking to camera.
options.looks_like: A medium shot at the desk or in the gym corner, eye contact, jump cuts and captions.
options.how: Tripod, Bluetooth remote, plug-in mic (not AirPods); ReCut pauses.

options.name: Walking or car yap
options.what: Talking while moving or from the car: a FaceTime-with-a-friend feel.
options.looks_like: Handheld walking through a market, or sitting in the parked car, glancing away and back. Candid and personal.
options.how: Action mode for walking; a MagSafe mount in the car; a wired or plug-in mic.

options.name: Graphic yap
options.what: Talking with overlays every ~2 s: chaotic, framed with headroom, or full-screen images.
options.looks_like: As you talk, camera-roll photos, screenshots and cards cycle over or above you about every two seconds.
weak_at: about 30 images per 60 s to gather
options.how: CapCut/Edits overlays; Canva for 9:16 full-screen images.

options.name: Podcast or conversation clip
options.what: A two-person conversation, clipped into shorts or sold with a teaser.
options.looks_like: Two people in three-quarter profile with big mics; the clip opens on the most contrarian line with captions.
weak_at: needs a guest and a set
options.how: Two phones or a phone plus a camera; clips reframed to 9:16 with the OpenCV tracker.

options.name: Pause-and-play breakdown
options.what: Talk over another reel that plays and freezes in a card, explaining each part.
options.looks_like: The source reel plays top-right, freezes and shrinks beside your head while you explain, then plays on.
options.how: A rounded-card overlay plus freeze frames in CapCut or HyperFrames.

dimensions.mixes: Briar reformats the same topics across formats (green screen, whiteboard, talking head, podcast style). A standard yap becomes a graphic yap in the edit.
dimensions.pick_by: Speed: standard yap. Personal and travel: walking or car. Teaching: graphic yap. Authority: podcast clip. Teardowns: pause-and-play.

dimensions.name: Length choice
dimensions.question: How long is the piece?

options.name: 6–15 s proof or vibe reel
options.what: Very short: one proof, one moment or one vibe, built to loop.
options.looks_like: One shot of the myth disproved, or a sunset with one line, ending on a frame that loops to the start. Viewers watch it three times.
weak_at: little room for teaching or CTA
options.how: End on a frame that matches frame 1 in Edits/CapCut.

options.name: 30–60 s value reel
options.what: A tutorial, tip or vlog with one clear payoff.
options.looks_like: Hook, three steps, a save moment and a CTA, all within a minute.
options.how: Script to about 120–150 words.

options.name: 60–120 s story or build
options.what: Room for story, personality or a full build; Rahul's typical reel is 55–75 s, and story-driven reels of 40 s–2 min work.
options.looks_like: A full PC build with every part and price, or a story with a messy middle and a lesson, over about 75 s.
options.how: Re-open a loop at about 15 s and add a pattern break every 15–20 s.

options.name: 2–3 min long reel
options.what: The longest reels (Rahul's sponsored 161–179 s), still under 3 min for recommendation eligibility.
options.looks_like: A sponsored comparison (dumb, normal, pro) with a full production, pinned to the profile.
weak_at: Rahul's 161 s sponsored reel reached only 0.17× followers
options.how: Chapter it with section cards; keep it under 3 min.

options.name: Long form (YouTube)
options.what: 8+ minute videos with a 15–20 s hook window and value spread through.
options.looks_like: A cold open, a promise, chapters with open loops, and value spread out rather than front-loaded.
options.how: Storyboard by chapters; record in sets; cut in CapCut desktop or VN.

dimensions.mixes: A long piece can waterfall into short reels of every other length.
dimensions.pick_by: Reach and loops: 6–15 s. Saves: 30–60 s. Trust and builds: 60–120 s. Sponsors: 2–3 min. Conversion: long form.

dimensions.name: Set approach
dimensions.question: Where are we filmed, and does it change?

options.name: One fixed signature set
options.what: The same corner, light and colours in every reel.
options.looks_like: A purple and blue wall wash, a warm lamp, a mic on an arm, the same tee. Recognisable at thumbnail size.
options.how: Mark the tripod spot and save the light settings.

options.name: Rotating sets as pattern interrupts
options.what: Several sets (desk, wall, booth) rotated every few minutes in long form.
options.looks_like: Each new chapter starts in a different place: a neon tunnel, a CRT wall, a desk. The scenery itself resets attention.
options.how: Shoot the chapters in batches per set.

options.name: Real places as sets
options.what: Evergreen spots (gym, room, desk) and temporary ones (an event, a trip) used as the backdrop.
options.looks_like: The tip is filmed at the squat rack, the next at the PC desk, the next at a viewpoint. The place is part of the content.
options.how: Gym etiquette and lens rules; lock exposure and focus; 1x lens in low light.

options.name: A backdrop that teaches
options.what: The background itself carries meaning: printed examples, a board, the products.
options.looks_like: Behind you, a wall of printed favourite ads or a shelf of the parts being discussed. The set does part of the explaining.
options.how: Arrange the props once and keep them out of the text safe zones.

dimensions.mixes: A fixed home set for talking reels plus real locations for B-roll is a common split. Rotating sets is the long-form version of switching layouts.
dimensions.pick_by: Recognition and speed: fixed set. Long form: rotating. Lifestyle niches: real locations. Expert authority: a teaching backdrop.
